summary: Modern databases have evolved far beyond storage and querying, embedding AI and ML capabilities directly into the data layer to eliminate costly data movement and simplify the AI development stack. By 2026, vector search has become a foundational feature across virtually all major data platforms, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities and adoption growing 377% year over year. Cloud-native platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks now offer end-to-end ML pipelines, LLM integrations, and semantic search natively, while PostgreSQL extensions like pgvector and pgai bring these capabilities to self-hosted and open-source deployments.

databases.name: Snowflake
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI is a suite of serverless AI and ML functions built directly into the Snowflake platform, enabling text-to-SQL, embedding generation, sentiment analysis, summarization, classification, and LLM inference without moving data outside Snowflake. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the AI Data Cloud with pgvector support, and Cortex AI integrates directly with Snowflake Postgres to provide embedding generation and text-to-SQL capabilities. Cortex also includes Cortex Analyst for natural language querying and Cortex Search for hybrid vector and keyword retrieval over unstructured content.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Meta Llama, Mistral, Reka, and Snowflake Arctic LLMs via Cortex AI functions (COMPLETE, EMBED_TEXT, CLASSIFY_TEXT, SUMMARIZE). Cortex Search provides retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. Snowflake Postgres with pgvector offers lowest-friction vector search path within the platform.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed by Snowflake credits per compute usage; embedding and LLM inference consume credits based on token volume and model selected. Snowflake Postgres is generally available as of early 2026 with pricing tied to compute and storage credits. No separate licensing required for Cortex functions within a Snowflake account.

databases.name: Google BigQuery
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data teams to create and execute ML models directly in BigQuery using SQL syntax, supporting logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, boosted trees, and deep neural networks. BigQuery integrates natively with Vertex AI to enable remote model inference, embedding generation via text-embedding models, and vector similarity search through BigQuery Vector Search. Users can call Vertex AI foundation models and Gemini models directly from SQL using ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions, enabling RAG pipelines without data movement.
databases.llm_integration: Deep native integration with Google Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, Flash) and Vertex AI foundation models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.EMBED_TEXT, and ML.UNDERSTAND_TEXT SQL functions. Supports external model endpoints and custom model deployment through Vertex AI Model Registry. BigQuery Vector Search supports approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference are billed per byte processed for SQL queries plus additional per-prediction costs for remote Vertex AI model calls. Vector Search queries are billed based on data scanned. Gemini model calls within BigQuery are billed at Vertex AI API rates (per 1K characters or tokens depending on model). On-demand and flat-rate slot pricing available.

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector data types and similarity search operators (cosine, L2, inner product) directly to Postgres, enabling semantic search, RAG pipelines, and embedding storage without separate vector database infrastructure. pgai is a complementary extension that brings LLM inference, embedding generation, and AI workflows into PostgreSQL via SQL functions, allowing calls to OpenAI, Ollama, and other providers from within the database. Together they represent the lowest-friction path to production vector search, handling up to 50 million vectors effectively and integrating natively with Snowflake and Databricks for hybrid analytics workloads.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension supports direct SQL-level calls to OpenAI (embeddings, completions), Ollama (local models), Anthropic Claude, and other providers. No application-layer middleware required for embedding generation or LLM inference. Integrates with Snowflake Cortex AI when Snowflake Postgres is used as the deployment target. Supabase Vector and Timescale offer managed pgvector deployments with additional AI tooling.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to self-host on any Postgres instance. Managed offerings are available through Supabase (free tier available, pro from $25/month), Timescale, AWS RDS/Aurora, Google Cloud SQL, and Snowflake Postgres (credit-based). LLM API calls via pgai are billed by the respective provider (e.g., OpenAI API pricing per token).

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables SQL-based inference against Amazon SageMaker models and Amazon Comprehend directly from Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL, allowing sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and custom ML model predictions without application-layer changes. Amazon Redshift ML uses SQL CREATE MODEL statements to automatically train, tune, and deploy ML models via Amazon SageMaker Autopilot, with results queryable as standard SQL functions. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector as a native extension, enabling vector similarity search and RAG capabilities within the Aurora managed Postgres environment. Redshift additionally supports embedding-based semantic search through integration with Amazon Bedrock.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference and embedding generation via SQL, and Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector supports embedding storage and similarity queries. Redshift ML connects to Amazon Bedrock models including Amazon Titan Embeddings and Anthropic Claude for text generation and semantic search use cases. SageMaker endpoint invocation is supported from both Aurora and Redshift for custom model inference.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML charges for SageMaker inference endpoint invocations at SageMaker pricing rates plus standard Aurora compute and storage costs. Redshift ML charges for SageMaker Autopilot training jobs (per training hour) and inference endpoints separately from Redshift cluster costs. Bedrock API calls are billed per token at model-specific rates. pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL is included at no additional cost beyond standard Aurora pricing.

databases.name: Databricks
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI and ML platform combining MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment; DBRX as Databricks' own open-source LLM; and Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks AI) for fine-tuning, serving, and evaluation of foundation models at scale. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in serverless vector database integrated with Delta Lake, enabling automatic embedding sync, real-time similarity search, and native RAG pipeline construction. The platform integrates with Unity Catalog for governed AI asset management and supports pgvector-compatible workloads through partner integrations including Snowflake.
databases.llm_integration: Native support for DBRX, Meta Llama, Mistral, and other open-source LLMs via Mosaic AI Model Serving. MLflow integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and OpenAI for LLM observability and tracing. Databricks Vector Search auto-syncs embeddings from Delta Lake tables and supports retrieval pipelines with Foundation Model APIs. External model endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) can be registered and governed through Unity Catalog.
databases.pricing_notes: MLflow is open-source and free. Databricks Vector Search is billed by DBUs (Databricks Units) consumed during indexing and query operations on serverless compute. Foundation Model API calls are billed per token at published rates (e.g., DBRX Instruct at approximately $0.75 per million input tokens). Mosaic AI Model Serving is billed per DBU for provisioned throughput or per token for pay-per-token endpoints. Costs vary significantly by cloud provider and region.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic search and RAG pipelines directly within MongoDB Atlas by storing vector embeddings alongside operational document data in the same collection, eliminating the need for a separate vector store. It supports approximate nearest neighbor search using the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) algorithm and allows pre-filtering by any MongoDB document field before vector similarity scoring, enabling precise hybrid retrieval. Atlas Vector Search integrates natively with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure OpenAI, making it a popular choice for teams already using MongoDB for their application data layer.
databases.llm_integration: Native integrations with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic Claude, Hugging Face, LangChain, and LlamaIndex for embedding generation and LLM-powered search pipelines. Atlas also offers MongoDB AI Agents capabilities and integrates with the broader Atlas Data Platform including Atlas Search for hybrid BM25 plus vector retrieval. Embedding model agnostic — supports any vector dimensionality up to 4096 dimensions.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above; not available on free M0 or shared tiers. Pricing is based on the underlying Atlas cluster tier (starting around $0.08/hour for M10) with vector index storage counted toward total cluster storage costs. No separate per-query fee for vector search beyond compute costs. Atlas Search and Vector Search can be combined on the same cluster without additional licensing fees.
